**The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** is a good fit for either appliance. Its **2,600 W AC output** is above the roughly **1,800 W** a single-burner induction cooktop can draw at full power, and its **2,073.6 Wh battery** gives you more cooking time than a small power station. It’s listed at **$899** in the [product listing](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop))

For an electric kettle, check the wattage on its label: it should be **no more than 2,600 W**. The station’s output determines what it can run; battery capacity determines how long. ([Home Power Facts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/induction-cooktop/))
